scientific.claim: For every \(0<s<1\), let \(\mu_s\) be the deterministic Salem spectral measure of Lai--Shi--Xie (arXiv:2609.22772v1), and let \(\Lambda\subset\mathbb Z\) be the canonical spectrum constructed in their Theorem 4.2. If \(C(R)=\#(\Lambda\cap[-R,R])\), then \[\liminf_{R\to\infty}\frac{\log C(R)}{\log R}=0,\qquad \limsup_{R\to\infty}\frac{\log C(R)}{\log R}=s.\] Equivalently, the lower centered mass dimension of this canonical spectrum is \(0\), while its upper centered mass dimension is \(s\). No assertion is made for \(s=1\), for Beurling dimension or lower discrete Hausdorff dimension, or for noncanonical spectra.
scientific.integrity: The proof is analytic and reconstructs the counting estimates from the source construction. No numerical experiment is used to establish an infinite statement.
limitations: The statement is proved only for \(0<s<1\).
It concerns the canonical spectrum in arXiv:2609.22772v1, not arbitrary spectra of the measure.
It does not identify Beurling dimension or lower discrete Hausdorff dimension.
Some comparison literature was accessible only by abstract or publisher preview; an equivalent specialized observation in inaccessible full text is a residual literature risk.

title: Intermittent mass dimension of the canonical spectrum of a deterministic Salem measure
